Hey [~accountid:615d90da9cdb93007288f515], there are only two options here:

# we engage a *courier who is registered as self-employed* - we need to check the registration with tax authorities, in this case, we pay directly to the courier; OR
# we engage *the fleet* that engages couriers (in this case, we have no direct relationships with the couriers, only with the fleet) - we pay only to the fleet.

We *cannot engage a courier who is employed by the fleet* even if there is a confirmation from the fleet about the existence of the employment agreement  - in this scenario, the *fleet needs to sign the service agreement,* the courier cannot sign the service agreement on the fleet's behalf. 

*!!!* If a courier does not want to register and we don't have a service agreement with the feel - we cannot engage him/her. 

Please let me know if this is clear and if you can change the practice in Lithanain accordingly. Also, please read the below comments from the tax team.

“Hello Martin,

Thanks for clarifying,

Working Environment Act (Arbeidsmiljøloven) does provide some protections for independent contractors like me, such as the right to refuse work, in this case declining trips I don't want to take.

[https://bolt.eu/no-no/legal/no/terms-for-drivers/ |https://bolt.eu/no-no/legal/no/terms-for-drivers/]- General Terms for Drivers [from 01.10.2022] says:

"4.4. Du har rett til å avgjøre når du utfører Transporttjenester. Du skal akseptere, avslå eller ignorere forespørsler om Transporttjenester foretatt av Passasjer, slik du selv ønsker." or in english:

"4.4. You retain the sole right to determine when you are providing the Transportation Services. You shall accept, decline or ignore Transportation Services requests made by Passengers at your own choosing."

As well here:

[https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4410730750866-What-are-Driver-Score-and-Acceptance-Rate|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4410730750866-What-are-Driver-Score-and-Acceptance-Rate]- it literally says:

"Drivers are always in full control of their schedules and the type of orders they’re willing to receive. That’s why they can always make a free choice to accept an order or not" and

"It is important to emphasize that drivers are always in full control to confirm journeys offered or not. The Acceptance Rate is thus never used to penalise drivers."

This is not taken out of context and screenshots attached.

As an independent contractor, I do not believe that my acceptance rate should be a relevant factor in this regard.

I have full control over which trips I accept or decline and I take this responsibility very seriously.

Therefore, I would appreciate it if you could provide me with a proper explanation as to why this ban occurred, especially if it is in contradiction to the terms and conditions of our contract.

It was very disheartening to receive a ban during the busiest time of the week.

As a professional driver who relies on Bolt for my income, this ban has had a significant impact on my financial situation. 

I am especially frustrated because I do not believe that I have breached any of your terms and conditions. 

Therefore, I am left feeling confused and unsure about what led to this action being taken against me.

I have noticed that this button does not always stop new requests from coming in, which can be frustrating and lead to a negative impact on my driver score.

This creates a difficult situation for me as a driver. If I accept a new request while I am still on a trip, I am then forced to cancel it, which can lower my driver score. On the other hand, if I decline the request, this can lower my acceptance rate.

I believe that it is important for the "Stop new requests" button to work as intended so that drivers like myself can manage their requests effectively and avoid negative impacts on their scores. 

I would like to continue working with Bolt and believe that we can resolve this issue in a professional manner.

I look forward to your prompt response and thank you for your time.

Sincerely,

# First, on *sending the comms from our behalf*. In this case, we would need the lead’s consent to send messages that would be considered third party marketing. For that, we could send the leads a message whereby we describe that we would like to send them information on getting assistance and training for a PCO license on behalf of a third party but we would need their consent for that. Depending on what channels you want to use, ask for data needed (like the email) and the following consent could be worded as following: 

_I agree to receive information on assistance and training for a PCO license provided by (name the third party) to my confirmed email on behalf of Bolt. I am aware of my right to revoke my consent by replying to this email. Further information on the processing is provided in the Privacy Notice for Drivers (add hyperlink)._  

Also note that the consent needs to be an affirmative action, like checking a box. The consent given needs to be logged and as mentioned above, the leads can also revoke their consent. For future references, it would be a good idea to add consent for the third party marketing in the general registration flow. If this is possible to redesign, let me know, so we can help with the wording etc. 

2. Second, when the lead is already on the landing page and is providing his\her details, then we need a *legal basis for processing the data they enter in the form*. We will have two purposes

* providing the data to the third party 
* collecting knowledge on lead’s status and assisting the lead internally 

We would use our legitimate interest as a legal basis for both but for that please provide transparent information under the details form on the fact that Bolt will be forwarding this data to the third party (name the third party) and the fact that Bolt will use this data in order to provide the lead with assistance, as well. We will conduct the legitimate interest assessments needed for internal documentation. 

The third party will be acting as a separate data controller since they are processing the data for their own purposes. Do we already have a contract with them that also refers to privacy matters? If not, then from privacy perspective it is not strictly necessary since they are data controllers, however it would be good to make sure that they comply with GDPR in their practices (maybe we could check their privacy notice?).

Also, please keep in mind that the data must be kept securely and deleted after you do not need it anymore.

# Max negative balance before messaging: When the driver reaches this negative balance, they will receive notification about low balance.
# Max negative balance before removing cash payment: This is the max negative balance the driver can have, once this limit is reached, they will get blocked for cash rides.

3. Now driver has to bring balance down to -150, to remove his cash block, (either through in app rides, where we will deduct commission and bring balance towards +ve or he has to pay debt). Once driver reaches -150, he can start cash rides again, but will be blocked again at -150.

However, I’m almost certain the following is happening:

* Before reserving a car Bolt Drive checks if there last T&C flow for a user, it is missing
* So, Bolt Drive triggers a new flow run and returns it to the user
* The user accepts T&C and in the Verification system, we move flow_run to {{PENDING}}. The Verification system process flow runs asynchronously, so the flow_run will be verified in less than 1 second but not immediately
* But if the user clicks the “Reserve” button too quickly, the flow_run will be still in PENDING, and Bolt Drive will return it to the user BUT the Verification system doesn’t support SDK for {{PENDING}} status in T&C flows


You can solve this issue in 2 ways:

* Treat {{PENDING}} as {{VERIFIED}} for T&C flows - but the user still has to do an extra click
* Use status callback from our SDK. For T&C flows on the app side check if status is PENDING and if yes - request car reservation automatically

**

{noformat}{{
  config(
    schema="ng_public_spark",
    materialized="incremental",
    incremental_strategy="merge",
    unique_key=["driver_root_id"],
    partition_by="activation_date",
    on_schema_change='sync_all_columns'
  )
}}


WITH global_multipliers AS (
      -- calculates global average multipliers per each number of days left in lifetime

	SELECT
    lifetime_1y_days_left,
    -- GMV multiplier
    AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur_avg,
    COALESCE(AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur),0) AS lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_avg,
    (AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur)+COALESCE(AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur),0))/(1.0*AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur)) AS flv_gmv_eur_multiplier
    FROM {{ source("ng_public_spark", "driver_lifetime_ltv") }}
    WHERE lifetime_1y_days_left IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 1
      ),

driver_ltv_adjusted as (
      SELECT
      l.city_id,
      l.driver_root_id,
      l.lifetime_1y_days_left,
      mm.gmv_model_accuracy,
      l.computed_on,
      l.lifetime_1y_start_date,
      l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur,
      COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur,0) AS lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_old,
      COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur * gm.flv_gmv_eur_multiplier, l.lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur) AS lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_new,
      COALESCE( COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur * gm.flv_gmv_eur_multiplier, l.lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur) - l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur, l.lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur)  AS lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_new
      
    FROM {{ source("ng_public_spark", "driver_lifetime_ltv") }} l
    LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_public_spark", "driver_lifetime_flv_model_metrics") }} mm ON mm.city_id = l.city_id
        AND mm.computed_on = l.computed_on
    LEFT JOIN global_multipliers gm ON l.lifetime_1y_days_left = gm.lifetime_1y_days_left
        AND mm.gmv_model_accuracy = 'immeasurable' -- only apply multipliers if model accuracy is immeasurable
        AND l.lifetime_1y_days_left IS NOT NULL  -- disregard multipliers for riders with 1y history
    WHERE l.computed_on = (select max(computed_on) from {{ source("ng_public_spark", "driver_lifetime_ltv") }} )
    )
    
SELECT
      driver_root_id
      ,MIN(DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date)) AS activation_date
      ,MAX(ltv_predictions.computed_on) AS date_compute
      ,MIN(CASE WHEN DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) < DATE('2016-01-01') THEN 0 -- we don't have GMV data for old cohorts
            WHEN city_metrics.gmv_model_used = True OR
            (DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) < DATE_ADD(current_date(),-365) -- THEN 'full LTV results for cities'
          AND DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) >= DATE('2016-01-01') ) THEN 1
          ELSE 0 END) AS full_gmv_available_flag
      ,COUNT(distinct ltv_predictions.city_id) AS cities
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_old) AS lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_old
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_new) AS lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur
      -- profit metrics are called simpliefied because they're based on expected profitability
      -- which is defined on the semi-yearly basis
      -- and is also applied in bulk to all gmv generated across a year
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur*COALESCE(pc.value,0.11))
        AS lifetime_1y_hlv_profit_simplified_eur
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_new*COALESCE(pc.value,0.11))
        AS lifetime_1y_flv_profit_simplified_eur
      -- Driver Revenue allocation 
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur * COALESCE(pc.value,0.11) * COALESCE(dra.driver_revenue_allocation,0.10))
        AS lifetime_1y_hlv_profit_simplified_with_dra_eur
      ,SUM(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_new * COALESCE(pc.value,0.11) * COALESCE(dra.driver_revenue_allocation,0.10))
        AS lifetime_1y_flv_profit_simplified_with_dra_eur


    FROM driver_ltv_adjusted AS ltv_predictions
    LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_public_spark", "driver_lifetime_flv_model_metrics") }} AS city_metrics
      ON city_metrics.city_id = ltv_predictions.city_id
      AND city_metrics.computed_on = ltv_predictions.computed_on
    LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_public_spark", "admin_system_city") }} AS city ON ltv_predictions.city_id = city.id
    LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_public_spark", "admin_system_country") }} AS country ON city.country_code = country.code
    LEFT JOIN (
      SELECT
      Distinct DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) AS activation_date_mapper,
      country.name AS country_mapper,
      MAX(Date(pc.month)) AS profitability_date_mapper
      FROM {{ source("ng_public_spark", "driver_lifetime_ltv") }} AS ltv_predictions --used to be rider profitability?
      LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_public_spark", "admin_system_city") }} AS city ON ltv_predictions.city_id = city.id
      LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_public_spark", "admin_system_country") }} AS country ON city.country_code = country.code
      LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing_spark", "rides_profit_rates") }} AS pc
        ON pc.country = country.name AND DATE(ltv_predictions.lifetime_1y_start_date)>=date(pc.month) AND variable = 'Profit'
      GROUP BY 1,2
    ) AS dates_mapper ON dates_mapper.activation_date_mapper = DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) AND dates_mapper.country_mapper = country.name

    LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing_spark", "rides_profit_rates") }} AS pc ON dates_mapper.profitability_date_mapper = Date(pc.month) AND dates_mapper.country_mapper=pc.country
    LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing_spark", "driver_revenue_allocation") }} AS dra ON dates_mapper.profitability_date_mapper = Date(dra.month) AND dates_mapper.country_mapper=dra.country
    --WHERE lifetime_1y_days_left is not null
    GROUP BY 1

Hi! Thanks for the info. I understand the changes. One important thing to mention is that there are two Orders in Romania that act separately. 

*Order no. 163/2021 for the provision of information regarding the presence of substances or products that may cause allergies or intolerance in unpackaged food products* is in force since 2021 and requires _indication of substances or products that may cause allergies or intolerance before purchasing food products. In the menu/menu list, panel, poster or screen, the price tag or the transport packaging, as well as in any informative material, after the name of the component ingredient of the food/drink portion, enter in brackets "contains:..." followed by the name of substances or products that can cause allergies or intolerance. Information on substances or products that can cause allergies or intolerance are written with different graphic characters from the rest of the documents, so that they are highlighted._

*There are many restaurants that do not add these allergens to each dish and thus rely on the message in the menu bar asking consumers to contact the restaurant directly to ask about the allergens* (photo attached). Because indeed the Order could also allow this practice: _indicating the place or the device through which the information on the substances or products that can cause allergies or intolerance is available or, if necessary, for additional elements, an information that invites the consumer to contact the staff of the unit_. 

*Order no. 201/2022 regarding the provision of information for the sale of finished products/food provided by collective catering units will enter into force on 15 March 2023.* It thus becomes mandatory to indicate the information regarding the type and amount of ingredients that exceed a weight of 20 g in the finished product or the food provided and it becomes mandatory to display the nutritional declaration and the additives used.

Since we are talking about two different Orders, the two issues: (1) allergens and (2) ingredients must still be treated separately. I mean, it's ok for them to be piled up in the list that the restaurant must provide, *but it's important that the allergens are properly marked and stand out, making it easy for clients to access them*.  

It's the restaurant's responsibility to add the allergens and ingredients, and the platform's responsibility to make that possible in the app.

Bug scenario:

# user performs Fraud Recovery internal verification, fails for some reason
# user clicks retry button, new verification (flow run) is started
# user submits verification data again, flow run reaches {{pending}} state, user closes SDK screen
# user immediately tries another order, "Verification Failed" screen pops up again, users retries again
# user submits data the 3rd time, verification from 3. became successful in the meantime
# verification from 4. fails because Veriff detects 2 submissions with same document - user is blocked

Root cause:
Fraud doesn't know there's a {{pending}} verification triggered from SDK retry

Fix:
Verification from 3. triggers a {{pending}} event, Fraud listens to it, registers the verification in its own DB and at 4. SDK will show "Pending" screen instead of "Verification Failed"

Hello [~accountid:619df385ef18ca00711f4974] [~accountid:5ecceffac761b10c33d5ba08],

On top of what Markus wrote before (which is correct), I added the following items that may be of interest:

* Marketing: user consent + notification to DPA; consent not required if data was obtained in the context of a prior transaction; lists of people who do not want to receive communications must be maintained; Bolt needs to ensure transparency.
* Interconnection of personal data (relationship of data in one file with data in another file(s), the controller’s own or the operator’s, for other purposes): can only be done with the authorization of the DPA, unless provided for by law.
* International transfers to appropriate countries: notification to the DPA.
* International transfers to unsuitable countries: DPA authorization + conditions Art. 34(1).
* Same corporate group: possibility of BCRs.
* Art. 35(6): if the processing is under legal obligation, only notification to the DPA, no request for authorization.
* Fines: between USD 75k and 150k, depending on the infraction.
* *Crimes are defined in the legislation*, with prison sentences in various situations (such as promoting the illegal interconnection of data or to whom illegitimately access data, among others).

Important: [Law 23/11 - On Electronic Communications and Information Society Services|https://www.apd.ao/fotos/frontend_1/editor2/110620_lei_23-11_de_20_junho-das_comunicacoes_electronicas_e_dos_servicos.pdf], Title III (On Privacy and data protection in electronic communications): some items *may be* relevant to Bolt’s activities.

About the meaning of “_means_” in the legislation: if you want, I can contact them directly in Portuguese to solve this doubt. However, my interpretation of the whole diploma means *it applies to Bolt per Article 3(3)* (mentioned by Markus below).

If you need any other details, please let me know - glad to help.

Hello there!

Apologies for the delay, we are currently running a backlog and a higher number of requests, hence some topics are a bit delayed. Sadly, I can’t offer you insight about verification itself as this is something that the verification team manages, however, I can offer you some insight into the fraud logic and fraud process that we have. 

The main idea of fraud checks is to assess the user and their risk. If there are some irregularities detected either through actions or relations, an additional score or decision is applied to the user based on this such as in every other product line we have. Business users in this sense are not treated differently, but they do have the additional factor of the business itself in play. Meaning the fallback for businesses with (for example payment problems) will add an additional risk for the user itself and this prompts the extra actions. 

Shortly, the logic is that verification as a method of recovery for the user is triggered once there are suspicious and irregular flags. The verification should be a *one-time* procedure which will end in either successful verification or not-ok (not passed) and the user will be then either trusted and the rules/restrictions relaxed or not. But if the user does not follow through (skips out) then it will be reoffered/pushed again. 

I could offer you information on how many users of the business payment methods we have determined to be “risky”. For more precise info about passed/non-passed verifications specifically can be consulted with the verifications team, however, I think they might not be able to split it by companies. While the company’s behaviour/history/actions add to the risk, the company itself is not “actioned” but its users are. 

As compiling, organising and pulling data is a more extensive request and this information is not easily accessible in this form you are requesting (requires work), kindly also state the urgency, potential impact, and reason for your request. _Is there an incident or issue that has brought you here?_ This way we can accurately prioritise and allocate the limited resources we have currently.

Having a quick look at this ticket on my day back after a week’s off and I would like to set expectations and that we agree on each team’s responsibilities when it comes to reviewing a contract, a document or an RFP:

* In every vertical, the *Business* is in charge of conducting the *first review* of the contract / doc and *make all necessary amendments to reflect 1. the correct way Bolt operates and 2. the agreed commercial terms* (we recommend in suggesting mode / track changes). Therefore, can you please do this for this Tender Doc?
* The business also usually send us a summary of the content of the doc, i.e. the term, the purpose, the total value or price. Would be great if your team could also arrange this.
* Legal then review the ‘legal provisions’, e.g. term of the contract, liability, responsibility, termination. 
* For anything related to *data sharing*, again it’s the Business that needs to have a go at filing in any information about data sharing (as you’re the best place to know what data will need to be exchanged between the 2 parties) and then a Legal ticket for the Privacy team needs to be created, so our colleagues from Privacy can review that all is in order from a GDPR perspective.

I hope this clarifies what we need the BB Business team to do in order for us to work efficiently together, but of course let me know if you have any questions. Thanks

Hey [~accountid:623d6f0eee1b5a007029efb6] Yes, it works. Would you like to get feedback on something specific?

The reason lies inside {{LockedExecutor}} which is called here: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/935a568152f5cb666f04de0a7f97fb712aa7b35d/src/foundation/monitoring/alerting_worker/main/service/RuleService.ts#L156|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/935a568152f5cb666f04de0a7f97fb712aa7b35d/src/foundation/monitoring/alerting_worker/main/service/RuleService.ts#L156]

The main issue is that {{ctx}} passed to {{lockAndExecute}} is reused inside of {{setInterval}} which is executed concurrently with the rest of the code: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/83ee8e57569f67f954d216dfb94a7cb92ec89fe9/common/alerting/LockedExecutor.ts#L26-L37|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/83ee8e57569f67f954d216dfb94a7cb92ec89fe9/common/alerting/LockedExecutor.ts#L26-L37] The same {{ctx}} object could be used inside of {{cb}} implementation, which means that if {{cb}} is in the middle of a transaction while {{setInterval}} is executed and the lock is extended, then there’s an internal request to {{/internal/extend}} while there’s a transaction happening inside of {{cb}}.

The fix would be to clone a separate context for {{setInterval}}. One way to do it is via {{FireAndForget.run}}.

{noformat}WITH order_times AS (
-- Getting order start and end time (from driver accepted till order completely finished)
SELECT ot.order_id,
  ot.driver_id,
  a.created AS order_accept_time,
  b.created AS order_finish_time
FROM ng_public_spark.company_order_try ot
INNER JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log AS a 
      ON a.order_try_id = ot.id AND a.city_id = ot.city_id AND a.to_state = 'driver_accepted'
    INNER JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log b 
      ON b.order_try_id = ot.id AND b.city_id = ot.city_id AND b.to_state = 'finished'
WHERE TRUE
  AND ot.state = 'finished'
  AND ot.created_date = DATE('2023-01-09')
  AND a.created_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-01-09') AND DATEADD(DAY, 1, '2023-01-09')
  AND b.created_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-01-09') AND DATEADD(DAY, 1, '2023-01-09')
  
), is_b2b_orders AS (
-- for each order, get all drivers that were in the distaptching pool
-- and wether they were already in an another order when they received the request (is_b2b)
SELECT egr.order_id,
    eg.city_id,
    eg.created_date,
    egr.driver_id,
    (ti.order_id IS NOT NULL) as is_b2b
FROM geo.eta_getetas_route egr
    INNER JOIN geo.eta_getetas eg ON egr.eta_token = eg.eta_token
    LEFT JOIN order_times ti 
      ON egr.driver_id = ti.driver_id 
      AND egr.created_at BETWEEN ti.order_accept_time AND ti.order_finish_time
WHERE TRUE
    AND eg.requested_by_service = 'search_auto_order'
    AND egr.created_at_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-01-09') AND DATEADD(DAY, 1, '2023-01-09')
    AND eg.created_at_date = '2023-01-09'
)
-- Aggregating is_b2b in the dispatching pool for each order
SELECT bo.order_id, 
  bo.city_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_b2b THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*) AS dispatch_pool_b2b_rate
FROM is_b2b_orders bo
GROUP BY bo.order_id, bo.city_id{noformat}

# When the user clicks the "Publish Now" button in Menu Editor, the HTTP call is sent and the next the screen is show without waiting for the HTTP call to finish. At this point we have an ongoing call to /publishMenu.
# The "Menu successfully published" screen is shown and the user can click the "Done" button.
# If they click the "Done" button they are redirected to the draft menu screen and a call to /ensureDraftMenu is issued (/publishMenu may still be running).
# If we're unlucky, the /ensureDraftMenu might happen just between the /approveMenu and /linkProvidersToMenu API calls from the the /publishMenu step.
# This means that the /ensureDraftMenu will see there's no available draft so it will use the previously published menu as reference (and not the draft that was just published).
# The /publishMenu call ends; so, at this point, we get a draft that doesn't match the most recently published version.

* Offering such a scheme to fleets seems acceptable - there is no reclassification risk because the fleet is a company; we will not make any payments to private individuals (drivers), and KPIs will be set for a fleet.
* Offering such a scheme to self-employed drivers seems risky as it might trigger reclassification risk, that is, if Bolt is involved too much in the driver’s service provision organization process, gives drivers instructions or controls the quality of services, the risk increases that the driver will be considered Bolt’s employee. However, it depends on KPIs - @Deivydas Katinas will KPIs be tight to the result (number of rides completed) or to the quality (such as driver's score)? The risk is much higher if Bolt imposes any quality controls.

Thus, it is advised to offer such a car financing program only to fleets.

If it is also offered to self-employed, KPIs should be tight to results, not the quality of services. In any event, any KPI we intend to impose needs to be assessed and approved by the legal team.

Resolved by using a larger value for the {{scanChunkSizeInRows}} [parameter|https://github.com/bolteu/change-data-capture/pull/1766/files#diff-ec353c98d6c06c130e1b35708d1317bf3f0c4945f227477f4a8b416963b2efcdR8] (had to [lift parameter restrictions|https://github.com/bolteu/spark/pull/1584/files] before).

Problem is that the current backfill implementation relies on PK values from the source table to be consecutive. This isn’t the case for these tables ({{min(id)/max(id)}} are about [1 trillion apart|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CF65PRL0N/p1677589258787799?thread_ts=1677489195.817129&cid=CF65PRL0N] even though the tables have less than 500 rows). With the default chunk size of 10 million, the backfill would issue 1 million queries to MySQL, with most of them for empty id ranges. Running these 1 million queries takes too long and the backfill job eventually times out.

So in essence you will pay the same amount then you would have if the objects were kept for the minimum duration, the difference being that some cost was pulled forward and billed earlier.Dividing the cost spike by the glacier costs in previous days it shows you are paying for an average of ~37 days extra storage. Here the good news is that you were able to remove such a large amount of data that you will not need to pay for storage ongoing so will certainly save money going forward.  By tomorrow we should have a complete new cost for a full day of s3 post deletion so we can estimate cost savings in the [future.In|http://future.In] terms of what could have been done differently. Your use of Glacier was valid based on the previous data retention policies and would have given a lower overall cost. Hi [~accountid:63622ea17d4645af4f03bd18] [~accountid:5a9eaf7ca00c7f2a80156a09]  I am sharing the feedback from the local counsel. Please let me know if this helps or if you have questions or I can be of any help.



*What is the legal framework for the police to send a data requests to Bolt? is Criminal Code / Code of Criminal Procedure a sufficient legal basis for the police to this end?*

The legal provisions indicated by the police indeed represent the legal framework for requesting documents and data, as well as applicable sanctions i.e. (art. 170, para. (1) Criminal Procedure Code, art. 170, paragraph (2), letter a) Criminal Procedure Code). They refer to the general obligation to cooperate with law enforcement in the case of a criminal investigation.Non compliance with such a request can under certain conditions be qualified as a criminal offence (art. 271 para. (1) lit. b of the Criminal Code). We analyzed this offence further within the answer to question 4 below.Interestingly, in this particular case, it is arguable whether a fine could be applied to Bolt. Art. 283 para. (4) lit. d) from the Code of Criminal Procedure, cited as legal basis, does not cover the handing over of data, but only documents and specific objects. Thus, applying it to non-delivery of data would mean adding new rules to an existing law, which is not permitted. Simply put, the Parliament did not correlate Art. 283 para. (4) lit. d) with art. 170 of the Criminal Procedure Code, leaving an unintended legal gap.2. - does GDPR limitations apply here? are there any local specifics we should take into account?This situation is regulated by both the GDPR and Directive (EU) 2016/680 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties, and on the free movement of such data, transposed in Romania by Law no. 363/2018.Under Law no. 363/2018, the police have the legal right to process personal data related to criminal law enforcement, including the categories of data requested from Bolt. Nonetheless, the police are also subject to the obligation for personal data processing to be lawful, i.e. necessary for the performance of a task carried out by a competent authority. This obligation mirrors the GDPR, meaning that Bolt is only obligated to provide such information which is necessary and [proportionate.To|http://proportionate.To] comply with the necessity principle, Bolt is only required to provide as much personal data as is adequate, relevant and limited to the purpose of sharing with the police. Bolt needs to be satisfied that the personal data is necessary for the police to fulfil its law enforcement purpose, as such Bolt may ask the police to what extent the information requested is necessary.Nonetheless, the mere volume of information is not an adequate reason not to provide it. Therefore, if Bolt is satisfied that the information is necessary in relation to an ongoing investigation, then the information should be disclosed.

*Is Bolt obliged to provide the information in case of such a broad scope as in the case at hand?*

The law provides in general terms the purpose of the data request. The police/prosecution is entitled to request any data they have reason to believe it might serve to solve the case, without limitation in volume.

As also mentioned under point 2 above, there is a condition of relevance. The police need to have sound reasoning to believe that the information they request could potentially help them. In other words, there needs to be some sort of logic / legitimate interest for wanting a certain type of information.

In the specific case, the police request itineraries for rides. You are correct in saying that this does not seem to have any connection with illegal access of computer systems and fraudulent financial operations.

However, there may be a reasonably legitimate interest, e.g. identifying the suspects. Hence, it is legitimate for the police to request information that can lead to the capture of the culprit. The itineraries might indicate their travels to and from their home, work place, hang outs etc.

*What are the consequences for Bolt/the management/ the employees - do the provisions mentioned by the policy indeed apply?*

As mentioned above, Bold might not face a fine, due to lack of legislation, but could be charged with a criminal offence under certain conditions.

Obstruction of justice requires:

* a criminal file to open and under pending investigation – which is the case;
* a refusal to comply with the data request – either explicit or implicit; Explicit means telling them directly that you refuse to give them the data. It is irrelevant if the noncompliance is for all or part of the data. In your case you tried to negotiate at first, but after the police gave you a clear answer that you need to give all data, any further attempts to avoid giving them data could be interpreted as an implicit refusal (i.e. that you stick to you original position of only offering 10 itineraries); Therefore, best to avoid any such discussion in the further. You could try to ask for more time, which should not be considered a refusal at first.
* the data request must be explicit and within the applicable legal framework – which is the case;
* there needs to be a prior warning from the legal authority in respect of the consequences for non-compliance with the data request – which is also the case – the police told you that you might face criminal charges if you do not provide the data.

In conclusion, further refusing to comply could expose Bolt to a potential charge. This could affect Bolt or its employees, depending on who actually refuses to cooperate (it will be determined whether it was a corporate decision or an individual one).

*We want to understand if we have any push-back solutions here? The options to force the police to narrow down the request?*

The ordinances issued within a criminal investigation can be challenged through a formal challenge. The challenge against the ordinances of the police are solved by the case prosecutor. Such a challenge could be taken into consideration if for example there is no clear legitimate interest for the data request, or the conditions for the request are not met.

A second solution would be for Bolt Services RO to claim that it does not have access or control over the data requested and that the data is under the control of an entity outside Romanian jurisdiction. However, given that up to this point Bolt has complied with the request, this would probably not be the best solution and would only antagonize the authorities.

In the case at hand, it is probably best to obtain a more attainable timeline, given the complexity of the request. In addition, we could also ask for the police to substantiate the relevance of the data, and escalate the matter to the case prosecutor. However, given that the criminal investigation is confidential, it will be very difficult to actually demonstrate the data is irrelevant or too broad.

*with* orders *as*

{noformat}with orders as 
		(
		select date(cot.created_date) as created_date, cot.driver_id, sum(ride_price) as ride_price
		from company_order_try cot
		left join admin_system_city ac on cot.city_id = ac.id
		where ride_price > 0
		and cot.state in('finished','client_cancelled','client_did_not_show')
		and retry_to_try is null 
		--and driver_id = 2446172
		and ac.id = 7 
		and date(cot.created_date) between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-12-31'
		group by 1,2
		),
compensations as
		(
			select c.date, ic.external_id as driver_id, sum(c.sum_with_vat) as compensation_sum
			from invoicing_compensation c 
			left join invoicing_compensation_data icd on c.id = icd.compensation_id
			left join invoicing_client ic on c.client_id = ic.id 
			left join fleet_driver fd on fd.id = ic.external_id 
			left join fleet_company fc on fc.id = fd.company_id
			where icd.compensation_id is null and c.sum_with_vat > 0
			--and ic.external_id = 2446172
			and date(c.date) between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-12-31'
			and ic.country  = 'hu'
			and ic.type = 'Driver'
			and fc.city_id = 7
			group by 1,2
			union all 
			select c.date, ic.external_id as driver_id, sum(icd.sum_with_vat) as compensation_sum
			from invoicing_compensation c 
			left join invoicing_compensation_data icd on c.id = icd.compensation_id
			left join invoicing_client ic on c.client_id = ic.id 
			left join fleet_driver fd on fd.id = ic.external_id 
			left join fleet_company fc on fc.id = fd.company_id
			where
			date(c.date) between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-12-31'
			--and ic.external_id = 2446172
			and ic.country  = 'hu'
			and ic.type = 'Driver'
			and fc.city_id = 7
			group by 1,2
		),
campaign_bonus as
		(
			select c.date, ic.external_id as driver_id, sum(c.sum_with_vat) as campaign_bonus_sum
			from invoicing_campaign_bonus c 
			left join invoicing_campaign_bonus_data icd on c.id = icd.campaign_bonus_id
			left join invoicing_client ic on c.client_id = ic.id 
			left join fleet_driver fd on fd.id = ic.external_id 
			left join fleet_company fc on fc.id = fd.company_id
			where icd.campaign_bonus_id is null and c.sum_with_vat > 0
			--and ic.external_id = 2446172
			and date(c.date) between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-12-31'
			and ic.country  = 'hu'
			and ic.type = 'Driver'
			and fc.city_id = 7
			group by 1,2
			union all 
			select c.date, ic.external_id as driver_id, sum(icd.sum_with_vat) as campaign_bonus_sum
			from invoicing_campaign_bonus c 
			left join invoicing_campaign_bonus_data icd on c.id = icd.campaign_bonus_id
			left join invoicing_client ic on c.client_id = ic.id 
			left join fleet_driver fd on fd.id = ic.external_id 
			left join fleet_company fc on fc.id = fd.company_id
			where 
			date(c.date) between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-12-31'
			and ic.country  = 'hu'
			and ic.type = 'Driver'
			and fc.city_id = 7
			--and ic.external_id = 2446172
			group by 1,2
		),
fees as 
		(
			select f.date, ic.external_id as driver_id, sum(f.sum_with_vat) as fees_sum
			from invoicing_fee f 
			left join invoicing_fee_data ifd on f.id = ifd.fee_id
			left join invoicing_client ic on f.client_id = ic.id 
			left join fleet_driver fd on fd.id = ic.external_id 
			left join fleet_company fc on fc.id = fd.company_id
			where ifd.fee_id is null and f.sum_with_vat > 0
			--and ic.external_id = 2446172
			and date(f.date) between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-12-31'
			and ic.country  = 'hu'
			and ic.type = 'Driver'
			and fc.city_id = 7 
			group by 1,2
			union all 
			select f.date, ic.external_id as driver_id, sum(ifd.total_fee_with_vat) as fees_sum
			from invoicing_fee f 
			left join invoicing_fee_data ifd on f.id = ifd.fee_id
			left join invoicing_client ic on f.client_id = ic.id 
			left join fleet_driver fd on fd.id = ic.external_id 
			left join fleet_company fc on fc.id = fd.company_id
			where 
			date(f.date) between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-12-31'
			and ic.country  = 'hu'
			and ic.type = 'Driver'
			and ifd.total_fee_with_vat > 0
			and fc.city_id = 7
			--and ic.external_id = 2446172
			group by 1,2
		),
refunds as 
		(
			select r.date, ic.external_id as driver_id, sum(r.sum) as refunds_sum
			from invoicing_refund r 
			left join invoicing_refund_data ird on r.id = ird.refund_id
			left join invoicing_client ic on r.client_id = ic.id 
			left join fleet_driver fd on fd.id = ic.external_id 
			left join fleet_company fc on fc.id = fd.company_id
			where ird.refund_id is null and r.sum > 0
			--and ic.external_id = 2446172
			and date(r.date) between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-12-31'
			and ic.country  = 'hu'
			and ic.type = 'Driver'
			and fc.city_id = 7
			group by 1,2
			union all 
			select r.date, ic.external_id as driver_id, sum(ird.sum) as refunds_sum
			from invoicing_refund r
			left join invoicing_refund_data ird on r.id = ird.refund_id
			left join invoicing_client ic on r.client_id = ic.id 
			left join fleet_driver fd on fd.id = ic.external_id 
			left join fleet_company fc on fc.id = fd.company_id
			where 
			date(r.date) between date '2022-01-01' and date '2022-12-31'
			and ic.country  = 'hu'
			and ic.type = 'Driver'
			and ird.sum > 0
			and fc.city_id = 7
			--and ic.external_id = 2446172
			group by 1,2
		),
daily_aggregation as
		(
			select 
			date(o.created_date) as "date", 
			o.driver_id, 
			coalesce(o.ride_price,0) as rides,
			coalesce(c.compensation_sum, 0) as compensations, 
			coalesce(cb.campaign_bonus_sum, 0	) as Campaigns, 
			coalesce(r.refunds_sum, 0) as refunds, 
			coalesce(f.fees_sum, 0) as fees,
			coalesce(o.ride_price,0) + coalesce(c.compensation_sum,0) + coalesce(cb.campaign_bonus_sum,0) - coalesce(r.refunds_sum,0) - coalesce(f.fees_sum,0) as driver_earnings,
			(1 -((coalesce(o.ride_price,0) + coalesce(c.compensation_sum,0) + coalesce(cb.campaign_bonus_sum,0) - coalesce(r.refunds_sum,0) - coalesce(f.fees_sum,0)) / coalesce(ride_price, 0))) * 100 as effective_commission
			from orders o
			left join compensations c on o.driver_id = c.driver_id and date(o.created_date) = c.date
			left join campaign_bonus cb on o.driver_id = cb.driver_id and date(o.created_date) = cb.date
			left join fees f on o.driver_id = f.driver_id and date(o.created_date) = f.date
			left join refunds r on o.driver_id = r.driver_id and date(o.created_date) = r.date
		)
select
date_trunc('week', d."date") as date,
d.driver_id,
sum(rides) as rides,
sum(compensations) as compensations,
sum(campaigns) as campaigns,
sum(refunds) as refunds,
sum(fees) as fees,
sum(driver_earnings) as driver_earnings,
avg(effective_commission) as effective_commission
from daily_aggregation d
group by 1,2{noformat}

*Setting reference:*

{{mysql-connect_retries_delay}}

The delay (in milliseconds) before trying to reconnect after a failed attempt to a backend MySQL server. Failed attempts can take place due to numerous reasons: too busy backend, timed out for the current attempt, etc. Connections will be retried for [mysql-connect_retries_on_failure|https://proxysql.com/documentation/global-variables/mysql-variables/#mysql-connect_retries_on_failure] times.

{{mysql-connect_retries_on_failure}}

The number of times for which a reconnect should be attempted in case of an error, timeout, or any other event that led to an unsuccessful connection to a backend MySQL server. After the number of attempts is depleted, if a connection still couldn’t be established, an error is returned. 

{{mysql-connect_timeout_server_max}}

The maximum timeout for connecting from proxysql to a backend in a hostgroup.
When proxysql tried to establish a connection to a backend, the attempts can timeout after [mysql-connect_timeout_server|https://proxysql.com/documentation/global-variables/mysql-variables/#mysql-connect_timeout_server] milliseconds and proxysql will retry to establish a new connection (against the same backend or another backend in the same hostgroup) according to parameters [mysql-connect_retries_on_failure|https://proxysql.com/documentation/global-variables/mysql-variables/#mysql-connect_retries_on_failure] and [mysql-connect_retries_delay|https://proxysql.com/documentation/global-variables/mysql-variables/#mysql-connect_retries_delay] .

{{mysql-shun_recovery_time_sec}}

A backend server that has been automatically shunned will be recovered after at least this amount of time. ProxySQL will not retry to use such a server again until at least the amount of time specified has passed.

{noformat}mysql> SELECT * FROM global_variables WHERE variable_name IN('mysql-connect_retries_on_failure', 'mysql-shun_on_failures', 'mysql-shun_recovery_time_sec', 'mysql-monitor_ping_max_failures', 'mysql-connect_retries_delay', 'mysql-connect_timeout_server_max', 'mysql-connect_timeout_server');
+----------------------------------+----------------+
| variable_name                    | variable_value |
+----------------------------------+----------------+
| mysql-connect_retries_delay      | 0              |
| mysql-connect_retries_on_failure | 5              |
| mysql-connect_timeout_server     | 1000           |
| mysql-connect_timeout_server_max | 5000           |
| mysql-monitor_ping_max_failures  | 3              |
| mysql-shun_on_failures           | 100            |
| mysql-shun_recovery_time_sec     | 1              |
+----------------------------------+----------------+
7 rows in set (0.00 sec){noformat}

{{mysql-connect_timeout_server}}

The timeout for a single attempt at connecting to a backend server from proxysql. If this fails, proxysql will try to reconnect according to parameters [mysql-connect_retries_on_failure|https://proxysql.com/documentation/global-variables/mysql-variables/#mysql-connect_retries_on_failure] and [mysql-connect_retries_delay|https://proxysql.com/documentation/global-variables/mysql-variables/#mysql-connect_retries_delay] . If none of the server in the destination hostgroup is reachable after [mysql-connect_timeout_server_max|https://proxysql.com/documentation/global-variables/mysql-variables/#mysql-connect_timeout_server_max] milliseconds, an error is returned to the client.

{{mysql-monitor_ping_max_failures}}

Monitor ping: It pings to all the backends, and success/failure is logged in table {{mysql_server_ping_log}} . In the case of {{mysql-monitor_ping_max_failures}} missing a heartbeat, it sends a signal to MySQL_Hostgroups_Manager to kill all connections;

Netting logic:

*Supply-side*

Everything in:

* {{invoicing_campaign_bonus}}
** is netted
** is automatic campaigns
** VAT sum available & applies
* {{invoicing_fee}} (with type = 'CustomFee')
** is netted
** is manual campaigns
** VAT sum available & applies
* {{invoicing_compensation}}
** is not netted
** type = ‘manual’ = manual campaigns, else automatic campaigns
** VAT sum available & applies

*Demand-side:*

Everything in:

* {{billing_document_invoice_document_row}} (with type = 'ride_hailing_discount')
** is netted
** VAT sum available & applies
* {{billing_document_invoice_document_total_adjustment}} (with type = 'ride_hailing_campaign')
** is not netted
** VAT sum not available because it doesn’t apply

Hey everyone,

* I agree with [~accountid:62382c1d562ab90069f6d424] that we need to issue the invoice/receipt from Bolt to driver if we want to charge parking fee from the driver.
* I am not quite sure if we need an explicit consent of the driver to set off the parking fee with driver’s earnings or the changes in T&Cs would be sufficient.
** formerly with respect to similar initiatives we have asked driver for an explicit consent for set-off with his/her earnings because otherwise, driver’s ability to drive on our platform would be restricted if driver does not agree to such set-off (we have found this problematic to defend without an explicit consent of the driver) - *let’s check finreg risks first, and get back to this one later*
* [~accountid:624469dd45ece00069c967bd] I believe the issues here are similar to the Booking Fee project and direct payment fleet project. The transactions regarding the parking fee here would look as follows:
** Bolt is offering drivers an incentive according to which they shall not pay the parking fee in the airport area if they have an active order
** since this is a campaign, Bolt is usually paying a parking fee to the Airport Parking service (Unipark) itself (based on the invoice issued by Unipark to Bolt)
** if driver does not abuse the feature, Bolt does not charge airport fee from the driver
** if driver abuses abuses the feature (enters the airport area without an active order), Bolt charges driver a parking fee based on an invoice issued from Bolt to the driver
** to make it more enforceable, Bolt intends to set the parking fee off with driver’s earnings (this should be based on driver’s consent to such set-off)

[~accountid:624469dd45ece00069c967bd] Do you see any finreg risks with this setup? Happy to jump on a call to discuss this. I can also draft a scheme of different transaction and payment flows, if helpful.

Happening because {{checkInternetConnectionInterval}} is set to 3 seconds whereas {{retryRestoreSessionEpic}} has a delay of 500 ms. Default value of {{isInternetAvailable}} is {{true}}.



This results in -
When app is launched with no internet, {{isInternetAvailable}} is true, hence every 500ms a request is fired. Total attempts of restore is 5, therefore in 2.5 seconds all attempts are exhausted even before {{isInternetAvailable}} is set to {{false}}, deleting the {{refreshToken}} and logging user out.

Ways to come around the issue -

# Reduce {{isInternetAvailable}} check interval to 500ms
# Check {{isInternetAvailable}} on load - requires changes in the common code
# Have 3 states for {{isInternetAvailable}} - true/false/undefined - requires changes in the common code.

*Responding to a claim form*Time given to respond to a claim form: you are given 14 days from the day of service (or particulars of claim if served separately) . Day of service is 5 days after the issue date (issue date 24 February 2023 + 5 days = issue date).*There are 4 options when responding to the claim:*Option 1: Agree with all of the claim: if we chose this option we must send the money claimed, including any interest and costs directly to the claimant (claimants address details are on the claim form). The claimant should receive the money within 14 days of date of service.Option 2: If we chose to agree with all of the claim and are asking for time to pay:we would need to complete the admission form (N9A) and send it directly to the claimant. In this circumstance (we do not respond to the court)Option 3: If we decide to admit part of the claim we must complete the admission form (N9A) and the defence form (N9B) and send both forms to the court within the 14 days of the date of service.Option 4: If we disagree with the claim or if we want to make a claim against the claimant (counterclaim) we must send a completed acknowledgment of service form or a defence form to the court within 14 days of service. If we send an acknowledgment of service we must send a defence to the court no later than 28 days from the date of service (essentially you are given an additional 14 days).As we are intending on defending the claim I would suggest we opt for Option 4 and acknowledge service, this will then allow time to prepare a defence (usually drafted in the form of a Witness Statement). I think this is the best route to take as we are still not in receipt of all of the information regarding the claim, I have responded to the person who raised the ticket and have also requested some additional information to get a clearer picture of what has happened, as this will help us when drafting the defence. ** the operator materially breaches the agreement;
** the operator is liable to pay three separate contractual penalties during a 30-day period;
** the allowed daily average of vehicles in the area is exceeded three times.
* The city does not guarantee that there is a sufficient amount of parking spaces for all vehicles subject to the agreement, i.e. this could lead to a situation in which the vehicles are parked in prohibited areas due to lack of space which in turn can lead to contractual penalties imposed on the operator or to parking fines and the removal of the operators vehicles and payment of costs related thereto. The contractual penalties under the agreement are EUR 1,000 per breach and, for exceeding the maximum number of vehicles in the area, 2 to 4 times the number of vehicles exceeding the limit times EUR 17,8.
* The operators’ vehicles may use at the maximum 30% of the parking space at a time.

* The liability of the operator under the agreement is not limited at all. The operator’s liability should be at least capped.

Here is what happens:

# Let’s say the user has set max_enrollments some time in the past
# Now user starts editing the form and removes the field (sets it to empty)
# User clicks Save
# The frontend checks the form data and sees that the value for max_enrollments is not set
# Because the value is not set, it will not be sent for the {{update}} operation
# Backend receives the payload without any value for max_enrollments
# Because it is a partial update, the backend will not perform any changes for that value (values not present in the payload seem to be untouched)
# Therefore, when the frontend fetches the updated data, the old value reappears

There are two possible solutions:

# Do nothing. Given that the field is now required, the user is no longer able to unset it. See this: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/TAP-1136|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/TAP-1136|smart-link] 
# Set the value to {{null}} and send it to the server. I tried that and it broke the entire Bulk group (it is no longer possible to see or edit it). The server returns this error: {{{"code":703,"message":"INVALID_RESPONSE","error_hint":"Response validation failed!"}}}. Obviously, the fact that you can send a payload that will make some entry unusable is wrong on many counts, but right now I’m unable to do anything about it because I don’t understand enough.

Hi Team,

I have initially consulted the issue with the external and here are the main conclusions:

* just for clarity - the Prague resolution does not set the conditions for the operation of carsharing in Prague, but only the conditions that carsharing must meet if it wants to use parking in paid zones (my understanding is however that this is crucial to have this access to operate the car-sharing, so the conditions must be satisfied anyway).
* +formally/legally+, Bolt Drive set-up through Bolt Services CZ would meet the condition of the RH and carsharing entities' separation set in the Prague resolution; however, the external cannot guarantee that the city of Prague will perceive the matter in this way (e.g. can argue that these are connected entities and therefore they should be qualified as one entity).
* the external recommends solving this issue in cooperation with the Czech Carsharing Association, which negotiated these conditions, and with the city of Prague; incl. requesting their interpretation. 

Please let me know if this helps or you have any further questions. Full expansion questionnaire can only be consulted once we have clarity that the proposed separation of the entities will be approved / not questioned by the city of Prague.



Full analysis below:

* *_Will launching Bolt Drive by an existing local entity (Bolt Services CZ s.r.o.) satisfy the Prague resolution's requirements?_*

_Firstly it is necessary to clarify the nature of the resolution you sent. This is a resolution of the City of Prague, which established the conditions under which carsharing (respectively short-term vehicle rental service) companies can use paid parking zones in Prague. This resolution was created in close cooperation with the Czech Carsharing Association, which negotiated these conditions. These are not the general conditions for the operation of carsharing in Prague, but only the conditions that carsharing must meet if it wants to use parking in paid zones. Therefore, it is not excluded to operate carsharing in violation of these conditions, but it will not be possible to use paid parking zones under favourable conditions._

_If you want to use paid parking zones in your business, you must comply with these conditions. The condition you are probably referring to in your question is stated in point 2, which excludes providers "combining carsharing and UBER-type services", which is justified as follows: "Due to the unclear legal qualification of similar services, it is not in the interest of the city of Prague to provide parking at a discounted price places to a provider that also provides a taxi service."_

_I would like to inform you that this resolution was adopted during the previous legislation, when ride-hailing services were not regulated by law and were provided in a gray zone. Formally speaking, the condition of point 2 is fulfilled if the carsharing service will be provided by a different entity than ride-hailing services. Your proposed model of ride-hailing operation through Bolt Operations and carsharing operation through Bolt Services CZ would formally meet the condition. However, I cannot guarantee that the city of Prague will perceive the matter in this way, I can also imagine the argument that in your case these are connected entities and therefore they should be qualified as one entity in the sense of the considered resolution (and therefore will not meet the resolution conditions)._

_I recommend solving this question in cooperation with the Czech Carsharing Association, which negotiated these conditions, and with the City of Prague. As the authors of the regulation, they could help you with its interpretation._

*  *_Bolt Drive will be available through the same Bolt app as RH (just different tap, separate t&c, etc. - as in case of the e-scooters rental service) - is this an obstacle?_* 

_Generally speaking, this fact is not problematic. From the point of view of the considered resolution, this question is also not regulated, so formally it should not be a problem. However, as a precaution, I also recommend consulting with the above-mentioned entities in advance._

# Quality metrics:

* We can impose quality metrics on fleets (legal entities) that employ drivers, because in this case we have no direct relations with drivers, thus, reclassification risk is low. 
* Whereas any quality metrics imposed directly on drivers (self-employed) add extra risk that a driver will be considered our employee. 

However, here I would like to align with [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2]. Branding terms are an extension of General Terms for Drivers. General Terms for Drivers (LT terms) clause 8 set certain quality metrics linked to the drivers account, that is, if driver _“does not raise total rating or activity score to the minimum required level within the specified time after receiving the relevant notification from us, Driver Account is automatically blocked”._

Would linking rating score to the bonus payment in practice pose the same risk as linking score to the activity of drivers account? If yes, the risk is already present. Or shall we treat it as a increased risk because quality metrics would relate not only to drivers' accounts activity, but also to branding bonus?

2. All global terms are available only in ENG for now. I advise to send to drivers (self -employed and fleets) who are already branding a email informative notice that drivers branding activities are regulated by Branding Terms available at [https://bolt.eu/en/legal/driver-vehicle-branding-terms/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/driver-vehicle-branding-terms/|smart-link].

3. If drivers are employed by a fleet, then the fleet is bound by these terms and need to ensure that its drivers are aware of them. If there is any violation, the responsibility is on the fleet as our direct contractor.  Since in cooperation with fleets, we don't have direct relations with its drivers, there is no need to have a branding terms specifically for fleet drivers (it is sufficient that terms bind the fleet). Hey [~accountid:63da287e790148a18093a774] [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2],

thank you for the feedback and insights! I will try to add more context.

1. Points about the car fleets - roger that. We already had a car financing project with the fleet (company), so more or less we already have some practice about it.
2. When we are talking about self-employed drivers, we don’t want to control them or have an impact on their quality of service and our main KPI is the number of rides. The driver decides to buy a car for himself and we can offer branding to him (stickers), plus (as a bonus) if he makes 5000 rides per year, then we can give him a compensation/bonus worth up to 10% of the car's value.
Another example, we are speaking with the insurance company at the moment and they are offering car breakdown insurance. Therefore, we thought, why not offer drivers who, for example, make 5,000-6,000 trips a year to pay for their car breakdown insurance? The main condition is that they make exactly this planned amount of trips. 
After all, we already have campaigns during the traffic peak, when we pay bonuses to the driver if they make the expected number of trips, which is provided in the conditions.

Now about the car fleets in Lithuania. [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2]  
1. Recruiting drivers is prohibited by Lithuanian law when we talk about ride-hailing.
2. Most car fleets simply rent cars. I would say we have around 70% or even more local fleets who work with this business model.
3. A small number of car fleets work under a contract/agreement, the basis of which is a percentage sharing of the income received by the driver.
4. Some of the car fleets providing accounting services to the drivers (basically they are doing it as an extra driver perk, not for the money from the driver pocket).

Have a nice day,

I have read the page on Direct Gov Website re acknowledgment of service see link [https://www.gov.uk/respond-to-court-claim-for-money|https://www.gov.uk/respond-to-court-claim-for-money|smart-link], I have also reviewed the Civil Procedural Rules. 

As we have decided to respond to the claim by disagreeing with the claim and filing a defence, Bolt must file a defence which sets out why the claim is being disputed. The defence to the claim must be filed at the relevant court and all parties under CPR 15.6 within 14 days of service of the particulars of claim Under CPR 15.4 (the claimant in this case served the particulars of claim with the claim form). 

However, in this instance we need additional time to gather the relevant information this will help us prepare and draft the defence. As we need longer than the 14 days we must file an acknowledgment of service and I would recommend we file that no later than today. 

Rules on acknowledgment of service are set out in CPR 10. General rule is the timeframe for filing acknowledgment of service is 14 days. 

In this case the Claim form was served with the particulars of claim on Bolt, so the timeframe that is relevant to Bolt is  14 days to respond as per CPR Part 10.3(1)(b)[https://www.justice.gov.uk/courts/procedure-rules/civil/rules/part10|https://www.justice.gov.uk/courts/procedure-rules/civil/rules/part10|smart-link]. 

Bolt was validly served on the *1 March 2023* - this is the date that the time starts to run. See deadlines below: 

# filing an acknowledgment of service is = {color:#bf2600}*15 March 2023* {color}
# filing defence to the claim = {color:#bf2600}*29 March 2023*{color}

I have diarised each date in my google calendar and set alerts so this deadline does not get missed. 

+*Repercussions for failing to respond to a claim form*+

* Failing to respond to a claim form may result in judgment being entered against Bolt - judgment in default 

In regards to your question about whether there are repercussions for filing an acknowledgment of service, the only obligation Bolt would now have is to ensure that the defence is filed before the deadline (as noted above).

Please find below our input on your questions below:

* *What is the legal framework for the police to send a data requests to Bolt? is Criminal Code / Code of Criminal Procedure a sufficient legal basis for the police to this end?*

The legal provisions indicated by the police indeed represent the legal framework for requesting documents and data, as well as applicable sanctions i.e. (art. 170, para. (1) Criminal Procedure Code, art. 170, paragraph (2), letter a) Criminal Procedure Code). They refer to the general obligation to cooperate with law enforcement in the case of a criminal investigation.Non compliance with such a request can under certain conditions be qualified as a criminal offence (art. 271 para. (1) lit. b of the Criminal Code). We analyzed this offence further within the answer to question 4 below.Interestingly, in this particular case, it is arguable whether a fine could be applied to Bolt. Art. 283 para. (4) lit. d) from the Code of Criminal Procedure, cited as legal basis, does not cover the handing over of data, but only documents and specific objects. Thus, applying it to non-delivery of data would mean adding new rules to an existing law, which is not permitted. Simply put, the Parliament did not correlate Art. 283 para. (4) lit. d) with art. 170 of the Criminal Procedure Code, leaving an unintended legal gap.2. - does GDPR limitations apply here? are there any local specifics we should take into account?This situation is regulated by both the GDPR and Directive (EU) 2016/680 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties, and on the free movement of such data, transposed in Romania by Law no. 363/2018.Under Law no. 363/2018, the police have the legal right to process personal data related to criminal law enforcement, including the categories of data requested from Bolt. Nonetheless, the police are also subject to the obligation for personal data processing to be lawful, i.e. necessary for the performance of a task carried out by a competent authority. This obligation mirrors the GDPR, meaning that Bolt is only obligated to provide such information which is necessary and [proportionate. To|http://proportionate.To] comply with the necessity principle, Bolt is only required to provide as much personal data as is adequate, relevant and limited to the purpose of sharing with the police. Bolt needs to be satisfied that the personal data is necessary for the police to fulfil its law enforcement purpose, as such Bolt may ask the police to what extent the information requested is necessary.Nonetheless, the mere volume of information is not an adequate reason not to provide it. Therefore, if Bolt is satisfied that the information is necessary in relation to an ongoing investigation, then the information should be disclosed.

* *- is Bolt obliged to provide the information in case of such a broad scope as in the case at hand?*

The law provides in general terms the purpose of the data request. The police/prosecution is entitled to request any data they have reason to believe it might serve to solve the case, without limitation in volume.

As also mentioned under point 2 above, there is a condition of relevance. The police need to have sound reasoning to believe that the information they request could potentially help them. In other words, there needs to be some sort of logic / legitimate interest for wanting a certain type of information.

In the specific case, the police request itineraries for rides. You are correct in saying that this does not seem to have any connection with illegal access of computer systems and fraudulent financial operations.

However, there may be a reasonably legitimate interest, e.g. identifying the suspects. Hence, it is legitimate for the police to request information that can lead to the capture of the culprit. The itineraries might indicate their travels to and from their home, work place, hang outs etc.

* *What are the consequences for Bolt/the management/ the employees - do the provisions mentioned by the policy indeed apply?*

As mentioned above, Bold might not face a fine, due to lack of legislation, but could be charged with a criminal offence under certain conditions.

Obstruction of justice requires:

* a criminal file to open and under pending investigation – which is the case;
* a refusal to comply with the data request – either explicit or implicit; Explicit means telling them directly that you refuse to give them the data. It is irrelevant if the noncompliance is for all or part of the data. In your case you tried to negotiate at first, but after the police gave you a clear answer that you need to give all data, any further attempts to avoid giving them data could be interpreted as an implicit refusal (i.e. that you stick to you original position of only offering 10 itineraries); Therefore, best to avoid any such discussion in the further. You could try to ask for more time, which should not be considered a refusal at first.
* the data request must be explicit and within the applicable legal framework – which is the case;
* there needs to be a prior warning from the legal authority in respect of the consequences for non-compliance with the data request – which is also the case – the police told you that you might face criminal charges if you do not provide the data.

In conclusion, further refusing to comply could expose Bolt to a potential charge. This could affect Bolt or its employees, depending on who actually refuses to cooperate (it will be determined whether it was a corporate decision or an individual one).

* *We want to understand if we have any push-back solutions here? The options to force the police to narrow down the request?*

The ordinances issued within a criminal investigation can be challenged through a formal challenge. The challenge against the ordinances of the police are solved by the case prosecutor. Such a challenge could be taken into consideration if for example there is no clear legitimate interest for the data request, or the conditions for the request are not met.

A second solution would be for Bolt Services RO to claim that it does not have access or control over the data requested and that the data is under the control of an entity outside Romanian jurisdiction. However, given that up to this point Bolt has complied with the request, this would probably not be the best solution and would only antagonize the authorities.

In the case at hand, it is probably best to obtain a more attainable timeline, given the complexity of the request. In addition, we could also ask for the police to substantiate the relevance of the data, and escalate the matter to the case prosecutor. However, given that the criminal investigation is confidential, it will be very difficult to actually demonstrate the data is irrelevant or too broad.

Ideally, we can set a “minimum dynamic commission amount” per market.

Since netting relies on the driver giving a discount to the passenger, the decision to net or not net needs to be made for each trip individually, at the moment the trip takes place. We will not know how much that particular driver will have earned at the end of the month. Nor will we know how much incentives to expect.

Setting a “minimum dynamic commission” will provide a buffer, so we won’t “overnet” into negative commission even if a driver unexpectedly ends up doing less trips.  

Local teams and the campaign team will know how much they’ll be spending on incentives in each city for a particular month, we could potentially leverage this data to predict ‘how much bonuses will still come in later during the month’. Perhaps we can extract this data from the campaigns settings?

Example: 

Incentives Spend for a month will be 50%

Commission for that market is 20%

Parameter: We set the minimum dynamic commission for that market to 150,-

----

one driver makes 1000 trips of 20,- each

Total trip fees: 20.000

Total incentives: 10.000

Total commission: 4000

Minimum Dynamic Commission: 150

Total to net: 4000-150=3850

Total not to net: 10.000-3850=6150

Previously we’ve been doing INNER JOIN to only take the users with existing LTV predictions. However, this could have impacted our CAC (since throughout the week new users would not arrive (because new users are only calculated on Monday each week), but spend would).

Now we have completed a LEFT JOIN. This will include all the users throughout the week, so CAC would be correct. However, with this we cannot calculate *AVG_Profit  = Total_profit / total_users* (because total_profit does not change throughout the week, while total_users does).

Therefore we should add a field where we calculate users only with existing predictions to have a stable relation of *Total_profit* and *total_users* throughout the week.

Thanks for sharing! Def. making notes for myself also for FAQ’s/playbook/sales team trainings. Some immediate comments:

* 3.2 - overall what is stated in the [playbook|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2923659743/Contracting+playbook+for+Bolt+s+General+Business+Portal+T+C.+Team+Account+Ride+Booker.+Standard+Customers] is to the point and largely sufficient. However I do agree that the part about “damage to 3rd parties” is somewhat debatable - in the end of the day it’s not like Bolt could base any claims on this clause if the damage is suffered by a 3rd party. However it might provide some supportive value if e.g. we are authorized by the 3rd party (e.g. driver) to claim damages/ penalties on their behalf. Also it’s for “educational” purposes so that such 3rd party claims didn’t come as a surprise for the Business customer - depends on the applicable law but I trust in most cases an employer at least is liable for damages and fines caused by an employee in relation to work duties.
* As for having the opportunity to influence the cost then obviously anyone can claim whatever but as long as they believe there is no causal relation between their activity and the damage created they do not have to pay. And then it’s up to a judge. 
* As for violation of Bolt policies then I can only refer to our core vertical Terms of Service here. If whatever is stated in these is clear enough to be enforceable towards consumers, it should be enough for Business customers.
* “What is acceptable/ what not” - _purposeful usage of Bolt services according to the T&C’s and the law without causing damage to anyone_ is acceptable - everything else is not. 🙂 
* Limitations to Bolt’s liability - sure, it is limited from the outset (to protect us from the unknown), but in all honesty there are not many cases to begin with. Difficult to harm a person with Bolt Business. As to the risks related to transportation services then that is what it is until there’s a risk/business decision to become more flexible. For the time being it’s take it or leave it and until the vast majority continues to take it then I guess there’s not much point for Bolt to absorb further risks.

hey everyone! 

I took a look at reseller orders in PT and indeed there are a few indicators of fraud. When the order type is reseller, there’s an automatic message that is sent to the driver with the passenger’s phone number. That’s how drivers identify orders that they can abuse, which they do by simply driving around after dropping off the passenger. I say that there are indicators of fraud because these postpaid companies are a bit tricky. We can’t say with 100% confidence what exactly happened, because there’s also the scenario where the passenger asked the driver for a long journey. We can only confirm it’s fraud once the company complains to us, that’s when we have a ‘payment problem’. If they don’t complain and pay the whole invoice, there are no losses to us. However, the indicators here are quite strong that it’s fraud and our advice is to reach out to these companies and check with them if it’s possible that passengers requested additional stops.

I pulled every reseller order since 01/02 where there’s no destination change and the final price is at least 2x bigger than the initial prediction. The list of orders can be found here => [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Gf9KCgKCvBMkKZwfaWDJJuLLmKV0ItEkW7S6CIzTPPo/edit#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Gf9KCgKCvBMkKZwfaWDJJuLLmKV0ItEkW7S6CIzTPPo/edit#gid=0|smart-link] 

I suggest that you go over the orders, especially the ones that have massive overcharges and reach out to the companies to apologize and compensate them by refunding the bad orders. I saw that there were potential big clients such as TAP, so it’s a good opportunity to build a good relationship with them. [~accountid:6215e9d79cd4a70071de651c] , can you cover this part or assign someone from your team to help out? 

In the sheet, it’s also highlighted the repeated drivers, which can be considered for blocking by the local ops. [~accountid:5b7bea09d08e47445d6fd01e] , can you take this part? 

To handle these cases from now on, we’ll use a fraud checkpoint that can recalculate orders at the end. Unfortunately, we can’t target only reseller orders with the input we have, we’re waiting on engineering work to have more info in the input to target more adequately. So our proposal is to recalculate every business order that doesn’t have a destination change and where the final price is at least 5x bigger than the prediction. I checked since the beginning of February and there were 37 orders fitting those criteria, with an avg of 1.85 orders per day, where the amount overcharged per order is on avg 76 euros. Our checkpoint will push those orders back to the upfront, which will have an impact on driver earnings and likely CS costs from the driver’s complaints. [~accountid:60e96a31131bf80069e1459f] , what are your thoughts on this strategy? Can we go ahead with it?
