I would say that this is very specific to a particular market / place of study but all in all, from legal perspective once you decide to do that, I would recommend you do the following to avoid any trouble:

* ask for a permission of the venue to film
* should you be conducting a study on the street, approach the local authority and coordinate traffic control and preventing accidents (including putting up necessary signs)
* print all the permits that you have acquired before the study and carry them with you during the study in case local authorities approach you

Please note that this might not be a requirement for every study venue but this would increase your chances of the process not being interrupted.

There are separate requirements for filming and interviewing people in public areas but since these requirements stem from the GDPR, I would kindly ask our group privacy manager [~accountid:5ecceffac761b10c33d5ba08] to contribute 🙂  As far as I understand, it is advisable to collect consents in a written form from the filmed individuals but if the area is too large and asking for a consent is not realistic, putting up big signs about filming before individuals enter the venue should be sufficient. In terms of interviews, the approach of collecting a consent before the interview sounds good enough. However, I’ll let Silja to advise 🙂

*Note for the QA:* 

The feature is controlled by the server feature flag (as it’s stated in the description) and there is no flag in the application debug drawer that you could manually change. After changing the feature flag in the admin panel you need to wait for at least 3-5 minutes so the changes are applied to a specific account.

When the feature is OFF on every app start there should be a message in the log:

{noformat}2023-03-14 10:31:44.716 [main] -> Comms - chat               I  Creating a default chat engine factory (null:7)
2023-03-14 10:31:44.790 [main] -> Comms - chat               I  Creating a default chat engine (null:7){noformat}

This will indicate that chat uses the old chat engine that Ride app used before we started migration to Chat SDK. A regular chat regression testing is needed in this mode, i.e just to ensure that no new bugs were introduced comparing to any previous release.

When the feature is ON on every app start there should be a message in the log:

{noformat}2023-03-14 10:30:38.734 [main] -> Comms - chat               I  Creating Chat SDK chat engine factory (null:7)
2023-03-14 10:30:38.751 [main] -> Comms - chat               I  Creating a Chat SDK chat engine (null:7){noformat}

This will indicate that chat uses the new experimental engine. This will require a careful testing of the following areas:

* Opening chat from different entry points: notification, active order menu, driver info menu
* Sending and receiving text messages.
* Receiving text messages with auto translation.
* Displaying a list of quick reply suggestions.
* Sending and receiving quick reply suggestions.
* Playing sounds when a message is received or sent.
* Displaying notifications for new messages.
* Displaying unread messages badge.
* Displaying correct chat info and updating it correctly if the driver has changed.
* Checking bad network connection cases (eg. sending messages when network connection is disappeared for a moment).
* Changing the app state to the background and receive messages.

If you found any issues or have questions please contact me directly in slack or send you questions to [#dev-comms-support|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CND9AL5LY/p1678698038315779].

*Research below contains the steps for applying to have a default judgment set aside* 



+*Relevant Application Form to file with the Court*+ 

* Defendant has to make an application to apply to have the judgment set aside, the form to use is N244 and the cost of this application is below:

|General application (N244) – by consent or without notice|£108|
|General application (N244) – application on notice|£275|

+*How to set aside a default judgment*+ 

* Under *CPR Rule 13.2*: the defendant making the application to set aside the default judgment will need to act quickly and will need to prove that the judgment was wrongly entered into. 
* There are three grounds for setting aside a default judgment. The first is a mandatory ground and the other two are based on the success of the application submitted by the defendant, however the judge has discretion when making a decision on whether to grant the application for relief from sanctions to set aside the judgment. See bases for setting aside default judgment below: 

# obtained as a result of the Defendant failing to file an acknowledgment of service or defence within the correct time frames but the conditions in *CPR Rule 12.3(1)* or *CPR Rule 12.3(3)* were not satisfied by the Claimant; 
# if the claim had been fully met by the Defendant prior to the default judgment being entered; and
# where the Defendant has applied for strike out or summary judgment and that application is still ongoing. 

*I*+*n addition a default judgment may also be considered to be wrongly entered into if:*+ 

# service of the Particulars of Claim or Claim Form is invalid;
# the Defendant filed an acknowledgment of service or filed a defence; and
# the Claimant applies for judgment in default of the filing of an acknowledgment of service (which was filed late) but did so after an acknowledgement of service had since been filed.

+*Other matters the court will consider*+ 

* The judge has discretion when making a decision on whether to grant the application for relief from sanctions to set aside the judgment. 
* The judge will consider the need for litigation to be conducted efficiently at a proportionate cost as well as adhering to the CPR rules and practice directions. 

*The judge will consider the following:* 

# If the application was made promptly; 
# the reason why the defendant wants to set aside the application; and
# if the defence has a reasonable prospect of success (therefore, the applicant must be able to show their defence would have a reasonable prospect of success and this can be demonstrated through evidence provided and supplemented to the Witness Statement)

+*What steps must an applicant take if they want to set aside a default judgment:*+ 

* Applicant must submit an application on form N244;
* Applicant must submit evidence in support of their application; and 
* Applicant can set out the details of the case in a witness statement (The witness statement should explain that you have acted promptly since finding out about the judgment, as well as the impact of having a judgment registered against you. The impact on the defendant could include difficulties such as: reflect poorly on the company's credit rating; moreover, it can have a detrimental impact on your personal credit score if you have given a personal guarantee to secure the credit).

+*Does the defendant have a good reason for not responding to the claim at the time it was served?*+ 

* The defendant must have a good reason for not defending the claim at the time, this explanation must be given in the form of a Witness Statement and include any supporting evidence.  
* See below for reasons for not defending the claim at the time it was served: 

# The claim was served at a previous address; (note: the defendant does not need to show they have a reasonable prospect of success if they have a good reason for setting the judgment aside, i.e. not receiving it); 
# The defendant was in hospital/out of the country; and
# The defendant was not able to obtain legal advice at the relevant time and was not aware that they had a defence (Note: this is only granted in exceptional circumstances).

+*Note:*+ The court may be reluctant to set aside a default judgment where the defendant did in fact receive the claim form/particulars of claim, however failed to defend it, especially when there has been a delay in making the application. 

+*When should the application be made*+ 

* Time is of the essence so you need to act quickly. When the court is considering setting aside a default judgment, the court will look at how promptly the defendant has acted. Whilst the CPR does not make clear what is defined as promptly, the judge deciding the application will use their discretion. 
* It is imperative to file an application to set aside a default judgment asap. Whilst delay may not necessarily mean that the application will fail the judge may refuse an application if the delay in filing the application cannot be justified. 

+*Relevant parts of the Civil Procedural Rules*+ 

*Cases where the court must set aside judgment entered under Part 12*

*13.2* The court must set aside a judgment entered under Part 12 if judgment was wrongly entered because–

(a) in the case of a judgment in default of an acknowledgment of service, any of the conditions in rule 12.3(1) and 12.3(3) was not satisfied;

(b) in the case of a judgment in default of a defence, any of the conditions in rule 12.3(2) and 12.3(3) was not satisfied; or

(c) the whole of the claim was satisfied before judgment was entered.

*Claims in which default judgment may not be obtained*

*12.2* A claimant may not obtain a default judgment—

(a) on a claim for delivery of goods subject to an agreement regulated by the Consumer Credit Act 1974^1^;

(b) where they use the procedure set out in Part 8 (alternative procedure for claims); or

(c) in any other case where a rule or practice direction says that the claimant may not obtain default judgment.

*Conditions to be satisfied*

*12.3*

*(1) The claimant may obtain judgment in default of an acknowledgment of service only if at the date on which judgment is entered—*

*(a)the defendant has not filed an acknowledgment of service or a defence to the claim (or any part of the claim); and*

*(b) the relevant time for doing so has expired.*

(2) Judgment in default of defence (or any document intended to be a defence) may be obtained only—

(a) where an acknowledgement of service has been filed but, at the date on which judgment is entered, a defence has not been filed;

(b) in a counterclaim made under rule 20.4, where at the date on which judgment is entered a defence has not been filed,

and, in either case, the relevant time limit for doing so has expired.

(Rule 20.4 makes general provision for a defendant’s counterclaim against a claimant, and rule 20.4(3) provides that Part 10 (acknowledgement of service) does not apply to a counterclaim made under that rule.)

(3) The claimant may not obtain a default judgment if—

*(a) the defendant has applied—*

*(i) to have the claimant’s statement of case struck out under rule 3.4; or*

*(ii) for summary judgment under Part 24,*

*and, in either case, that application has not been dealt with;*

*(b) the defendant has satisfied the whole claim (including any claim for costs) on which the claimant is seeking judgment;*

*(c)*

*(i) the claimant is seeking judgment on a claim for money; and*

*(ii) the defendant has filed or served on the claimant an admission under rule 14.4 or 14.7 (admission of liability to pay all of the money claimed) together with a request for time to pay; or*

*(d) notice has been given under rule 82.21 of a person’s intention to make an application for a declaration under section 6 of the Justice and Security Act 2013(2) in relation to the proceedings, and that application has not been dealt with.*

(Part 14 sets out the procedure where a defendant admits a money claim and asks for time to pay.)

(Rule 6.17 provides that, where the claim form is served by the claimant, the claimant may not obtain default judgment unless a certificate of service has been filed.)

Jana if you mean examples of cases when like you mentioned “know local traffic and conditions”.

Here are some typical examples of signals on driver score when it’s good to have more knowledge/better analysis of the local conditions:

* rider_cancelled_before_pickup_driver_not_moving
* rider_cancelled_before_pickup_driver_moving_to_wrong_direction
* driver_cancelled_before_pickup_client_ordered_to_forbidden_area

The first two ones it can be important to be a bit more knowledgeable, as there are reasons why the driver may not be moving (accepted order while at a very busy location), and situations where the driver might move in the wrong direction to in a quicker/better way get to the customer. 

And for longer routes there are situations when drivers should be taking one that isn’t the recommended, for example traffic incidents.

For the last one good to have knowledge of where drivers can pick customers up, and be able to analyze the map. There are of course situations where this is a correct cancel reason, especially when the driver cant get close enough to get the cancel fee.

About this:

*_There are no specifications on what is considered to be rejected or canceled orders and the mentioned KB/FAQ articles do not explain well which of the ratings are actually influenced in case the driver first accepts the order and only cancels it after._*

In the [self-help article |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4413999533586](also linked to the BQS - Backend KB article), there’s a list of situations that negatively affect the driver score:

* Rider cancels the trip as you are not moving toward the pick-up point
* Rider cancels the trip after you have picked them up due to safety concerns
* You start the trip before the rider has entered the vehicle
* *You cancel the trip before reaching the pick-up point*
* *You cancel the trip after reaching the pick-up point without calling or messaging the rider*
* Rider gives you a 1 or 2-star rating due to cleanliness, conduct or safety concerns
* Rider raises a concern about health, safety or other similar topic after the trip.

So if the driver has already accepted the trip, but cancels it a) before they reach the pick-up point or b) after they reach the pick-up point and did not call/message the rider.

some follow-up comments concerning this topic - it turned out that there is no clarity which entity should be perceived as operating Bolt RH business in CZ - Bolt Services CZ or Bolt Operations OÜ:

* From the point of view of trade law, ridehailing should be operated by the entity Bolt Services CZ s.r.o., which has a trade license with the title: "Trade and service mediation". Bolt Operations OÜ does not have this license - if it were to have it, it would be necessary to establish its so-called registered branch in the Czech Republic. There are also opinions that a trade license can be obtained even for a foreign company without a registered branch, but this is questionable in the opinion of the trade authorities.
* However, from the point of view of the terms and conditions, it is questionable which entity is the "taxi service intermediary", i.e. the ridehailing operator - see definition 1.1. of T&Cs, from which it is not clear whether the intermediary of the taxi service is Bolt Operations OÜ or another Bolt group company (= Bolt Services CZ s.r.o.). From the invoices it also appears that ridehailing operator is Bolt Operations OÜ.

Car sharing requires a trade license called "Rental and lending of movable property" (the carsharing business is basically renting cars for a fixed period). This trade license is currently owned by Bolt Services CZ s.r.o. - the company is thus formally already ready to start carsharing activities (were it not for the requirements arising from the Prague resolution). However, if we would like to operate through a foreign entity (Bolt Operations), we need to secure a registered branch in CZ that will have a trade license.

# Registration with the 3 Regions in Belgium 
# Declaration of all cells and batteries and pay the necessary fees
# Provide awareness and prevention campaign
# Collect & transport according to ADR regulations
# Recycle by an authorized and approved recycling company
# Demonstrate and submit recycling effectiveness
# Reporting to the 3 Regions

So even with another recycling partner we would still have many steps left.

Overall looks very promising, but require some changes on our side to start using it even on some prelive clusters (requires kafka to run on Java 11 + adding some custom monitoring jars).

It supports quite a lot of rebalancing approaches (rack-awareness, resource utilization balance, based on predefined targets, etc). 

It also significantly simplify operations, since it allows to move all leaders from the target broker in advance. It exposes REST API for all operations, so could be easily integrated with our maintenance playbooks (e.g. for rolling restart). Due to this it also significantly simplify adding/removing brokers, due to automatic rebalancing.

There is also quite decent UI. 

From security perspective it supports both authentication and authorization (with viewer/user/admin roles) and 2 step verification for POST requests (request is sent initially, got reviewed by someone, approved and applied).



Right now the plan is to proceed with kafka and java upgrade EPIC, afterwards we could think about some architectural setup for prelive clusters.

Client contacted us, that she received a Telegram message from an unknown number. When client tried to find out more - who is this person, he replied that “have you ever faced with a delivery problem, apartment 3 and second floor”As she believed it was our courier who has previously delivered order to her.

*_Internal_*: After our own investigation, we found out that one of the couriers was illegally sharing his courier account with another person. We checked the phone number from which client received those messages - and it actually was one of our leads who was constantly rejected in our partnership. So the person who was renting the courier account - was actually delivering order to client and after some time confronted her with text messages on Telegram. At that time we didn’t have a phone masking feature. So these situations were happening time by time.Steps taken from our side - blocked courier profile that was illegally sharing his account and made sure that we never accept a partnership with the person who contacted this client.

But now - after two months we received the following message from the client

*The message from the client:*

To whomever it might concern,
Unfortunately, I have not received any answer from you regarding the below-mentioned issue. As I mentioned in my first email, what has happened to me is directly connected to a breach of GDPR on your part, and after talking about my story publicly, I have learned that the same issue has happened to multiple people, which leads me to believe that you should be aware of the situation and of how it is persisting.


In one of your emails, you stated that “they will not be able to see your phone number, even if they call you (or you call them) via the application. The phone number they (and you) will see in your phone when making this phone call will be replaced with our phone number which is acting as a proxy.“, however, during my time using Bolt, I have only ever received calls via normal phone and used that same phone number to contact or be contacted via message as well. All of these numbers are in my “incoming calls” list on my phone, and when I called any of these numbers by mistake, people would actually answer. 

A simple test to see that at least one phone number is not a proxy number is the phone number of the alleged delivery man who saved my information. I saved his number on my phone after what happened to see if I would be able to see his information on Whatsapp, and there is a Whatsapp account connected to this number, however, without information. As we both know, in order to have WhatsApp, the application must be downloaded and connected with a phone number; therefore, either you create a WhatsApp account for each proxy number that was ever used for the deliveries, or this number is a real number.
From my side, in these months, I have contacted the police, which has started an investigation from their side that unfortunately hasn’t led to any conclusions since there were no information about this person, but I have also personally started a research about what to do in case of GDPR infringement.

As per the European Commission site, “You can claim compensation if a company or organisation hasn’t respected the data protection law and you’ve suffered material damages (for example financial loss) or non-material damages (for example distress or loss of reputation). [...]” (source: [https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/reform/rights-citizens/redress/can-i-claim-compensation_en|https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/reform/rights-citizens/redress/can-i-claim-compensation_en|smart-link] ), and, after further research, I found that the claim for compensation in this case, when the damage is General Psychiatric affecting my daily life and my personal mental wellbeing, goes from ~1,743 EUR to ~6,634 EUR (source: [https://www.legalexpert.co.uk/data-breach-compensation/uk-gdpr-breach-compensation-calculator/|https://www.legalexpert.co.uk/data-breach-compensation/uk-gdpr-breach-compensation-calculator/|smart-link] ), therefore, considering the amount of stress I was put under due to this situation and the effects that it had on me (I am still not able to walk alone without feeling unease), I request a compensation of at least 1,750 EUR.

In case this request is not complied with, please note that it is my right to contact the Data State Inspectorate and bring the matter to court on top of contacting the Local Consumer Rights Institution (PTAC), but I truly hope that this will not be necessary.
Unfortunately, none of us is able to check or control the behavior of third parties; if it wouldn’t have been this specific person saving my information and using them to contact me and harass me, it would have been someone else. What we should do, though, is make sure that these type of issues do not happen. When customers open an account with a platform like yours, they give you their trust with their personal data, and you are obliged to keep such data safe under EU law. If such instances happen on multiple occasions, it means that it was not a one-time occurence, where one specific person was able to save the customer’s information somehow, but it means that there is a hole in the system, and untill it is fixed, many more people will have to go through what I did, and some of them might not be as lucky as me.
Awaiting an answer,
Carlotta Frascadore.

I am not an expert in planning permission, but the property agent should be. 

* The Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order categorises uses of land and buildings. 
* Developments may not be used for purposes that are not within the use class for which they received planning permission.
* Sui generis = “of its own” use class.
* Taxi businesses require sui generis planning permission under this legislation.
* Most administrative businesses use the defunct use class of B or the new use class of E. 

As a taxi business, we need to be able to apply for sui generis planning permission to use the property. Therefore, what we need the landlord/lessor to confirm is that they are okay with us using the office for our taxi business and consent to us applying for the sui generis use class for the office (not the building).

We also charge a Cashout fee in the UK, and, according to the local legislation, we are allowed to do so as long as this fee is used to cover the Cashout-related expenses.

The Cashout expenses consist of:

* operational expenses (including development and customer  support)
* liquidity buffer
* monetary loss related to keeping the funds on the account instead of investment

Here is an example of the cost calculation for the UK: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/4064837842/Early+Cashout+UK+-+Cost+Model|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/4064837842/Early+Cashout+UK+-+Cost+Model|smart-link] I will create the same for Ukraine. 

TL;DR: Essentially, we are not charging the drivers any extra money in order to increase our revenue, but use this money to cover the Cashout-related costs. Cashouts are different from payouts in the sense that we pay to the driver beforehand, before the card payment reaches our account (since Adyen payouts take minimum 24 hours). So, by providing Cashouts, we lose money, and we need to compensate for this loss.

I believe, you are the best specialist, familiar with the local legislation. Is there anything that may prevent us from charging the cost of operations?

I have reviewed the DVLA guide on ‘Assessing Fitness to Drive’ chapter 3, which outlines the requirements for individuals who have a diagnosis of Diabetes.

I also note on SLACK that Bolt have recently received a letter from the Drivers local MP. I have tried to gather information from Diabetes UK, DVLA and ACAS (however, please note, I did not give any information about where I was calling from and did not provide them with any personal details, I simply called for generic advice/guidance).

Diabetes UK have said that provided a person meets the requirements of the DVLA then there is no issue for them to continue to drive as the relevant medical assessments would have taken place.

ACAS also reiterated the above and stated that the DVLA guidance must be followed as the DVLA guidance is drafted in conjunction with legislation.

Whilst the Driver is an independent contractor and is therefore not protected by Employment Law Legislation, the Driver still gains protection under the Equality Act.

After reviewing the letter received from the Local MP it seems that this may have been an admin error on the DVLA system, which has now been rectified. Essentially, if the Driver is in possession of a full DVLA licence and has been deemed fit to drive by the DVLA, it may be considered disproportionate/discriminatory if he is blocked from the App, and this is because the driver has satisfied the DVLA protocol. Unless there is some other reason the driver was blocked that I have missed, if this is the case, this may need to be approached differently.

I have also reviewed Bolt T&C’s for drivers and in particular clause 8 and there is no specific mention of terminating use of the platform on the grounds of a medical condition, however there is reference to when there is a health and safety concern under 8(d)(ii).

Hi [@rade.njezic|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U02Q21P58A3],
I've talked to several senior members of the policy team and they have concerns about the initiative.Here is some of the concerns:

* Some EU countries are very privacy sensitive (Germany, France...) so I’m not sure the US examples of Uber or Lyft can be fully followed in the EU. Hence, there is a legal need to check with regulations in EU member states if this is even possible.
* There is a strong concern about how the users will react. Hence, there should at least be an option to opt out in the app.
* Bolt is just about to introduce trip audio recording testing - having those two processes communicated (or risking them both being communicated around the same time) might amplify potential reputational risks around our perceived approach towards data privacy.

I will get back to you if more positions is presented, but as stated, policy members are concerned.

Since this ticket was handled with our external advisors in Denmark I will close this ticket. 

For future cases, the termination template and response from the law firm is included below: 

_“According to the Danish Act on Post-Termination Restrictions section 10(1) and the employment contract p. 8, the non-compete clause may be terminated by the employer with one month’s notice to expire at the end of a month. The employee will be entitled to a lump sum (60% of two months’ salary)._

_An employee cannot waive a non-compete clause or in any other way terminate the non-compete clause. However, the parties can agree in a severance agreement that the non-compete clause shall not be enforced and that the employee is not entitled to compensation. This requires that the severance agreement is entered in both parties’ interests and that it is balanced for both parties. If the employee does not want to enter into such agreement, e.g., because the employee will not be entitled to a lump sum, then the employer must terminate the non-compete clause with one month’s notice in accordance with the Danish Act on Post-Termination.”_

For the avoidance of doubt, including a non-compete clause in an employment agreement for a Danish employee will always provide the employee with a right to lump sum compensation regardless if the non-compete is waived or remains valid after the termination of the employment.

[~accountid:639b20bdf78d12c0f471a5e4] Unfortunately with the Workday Flow it is actually using two different data sources for both of these transactions. 

* Bolt Finance Inventory Stock Requests_V2 - for this one it is taking the put-away date transaction, which means the point in which the mechanic actually clicked to add the stock into their inventory to signify that the stock request was completed and received. 
* Bolt Finance Inventory Stock Requests_CMR - this report highlights whether the closed delivery tickets (i.e. proof of delivery) was completed and whether any documents were attached to the relevant tickets themselves. 

The way that Workday has designed this (which we have no control over) is that when an Inventory Shipment is created, it then splits off into two branches - Put/Away and Delivery Ticket which are treated as two separate objects in the system. So combining them won’t be possible, as if we went back using the data sources together it might not give an accurate image of a ticket that was completed, but maybe put-away not done.
